National Register of Historic Places listings in Cleveland
National Register of Historic Places listings in Cuyahoga County, Ohio

stops.name: Soldiers' and Sailors' Monument
stops.description: Cuyahoga County's Civil War memorial has stood in the southeast quadrant of Public Square since 1894, and the names of some 9,000 local soldiers and sailors are cut into the marble tablets inside it.

stops.name: Terminal Tower
stops.description: Built over a railroad station by the Van Sweringen brothers and finished in 1930, this 52-story tower was the tallest building outside New York City for a quarter of a century.

stops.name: Old Stone Church
stops.description: The oldest building still standing on Public Square, this Presbyterian congregation has held the same corner since 1820 and rebuilt twice after fires.

stops.name: Hotel Cleveland
stops.description: Opened in 1918 on a corner that has held an inn since a tavern stood here in 1815, and later folded into the Terminal Tower complex next door.

stops.name: Cleveland Arcade
stops.description: A glass-roofed shopping arcade from 1890, five levels of brass railings under a skylight, and one of the first indoor shopping centers built in the United States.

stops.name: Cleveland Trust Company Building
stops.description: The 1908 bank rotunda under a stained glass dome now holds a grocery store, so you can buy a sandwich standing where the tellers once counted money.

stops.name: Playhouse Square
stops.description: Five theaters opened along this block within sixteen months in the early 1920s, went dark in the 1970s, and were saved to become the largest performing arts center in the country outside Lincoln Center.

stops.name: Grays Armory
stops.description: A turreted sandstone fortress finished in 1894 for the Cleveland Grays militia company, and the last of the city's downtown armories still standing.

stops.name: Erie Street Cemetery
stops.description: Cleveland's oldest surviving burial ground, opened in 1826 on what was then the edge of town and now hemmed in by the ballpark and the freeway.

stops.name: Cleveland Public Library Main Library
stops.description: The 1925 Beaux Arts main library was laid out as a twin to the courthouse block, and its Eastman Reading Garden is an open air room in the middle of downtown.

stops.name: Fountain of Eternal Life
stops.description: Marshall Fredericks's bronze figure rising out of flame on Veterans Memorial Plaza, dedicated in 1964 to Cleveland's war dead and known locally as the War Memorial Fountain.

stops.name: Cuyahoga County Courthouse
stops.description: The Beaux Arts county courthouse of 1912 closes the north end of the Mall, and the statues of lawgivers on its front steps were part of the original Group Plan for downtown.

stops.name: Cleveland City Hall
stops.description: City Hall opened in 1916 as the twin of the county courthouse across the Mall, and its marble rotunda is open to anyone who walks in the front door.

stops.name: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
stops.description: I. M. Pei's glass pyramid on the lakefront opened in 1995, put here because a Cleveland disc jockey is credited with popularizing the phrase rock and roll.

stops.name: Great Lakes Science Center
stops.description: The lakefront science museum keeps the NASA Glenn Visitor Center inside it, including the Apollo command module that flew the Skylab 3 crew.

note: Cleveland has never come up in this rotation, so it wins outright. All fifteen stops sit inside the downtown core, running Public Square to Euclid Avenue to the Mall to North Coast Harbor, which is a walkable loop of roughly two miles. Two stops carry a null address and a null ZIP on purpose: the Fountain of Eternal Life stands on Veterans Memorial Plaza and the Cuyahoga County Courthouse stretches along Lakeside Avenue, and neither Wikipedia nor the NRHP rows give either one a house number, so nothing was invented. Every other ZIP was looked up from the verified street address. Dropped as outliers across the Cuyahoga River: West Side Market (1979 W 25th St) and the Hope Memorial Bridge with its Guardians of Traffic pylons, both good stops but roughly a mile past the edge of this cluster, so they are worth a second Cleveland batch rather than a detour in this one. Also dropped: USS Cod Submarine Memorial (1201 N Marginal Rd, 44114) verified fine but sits east of the harbor cluster, and Public Auditorium (500 Lakeside Ave, 44114) which duplicates the City Hall and Mall block. The Free Stamp sculpture in Willard Park has no Wikipedia article of its own, so it was left out.
